questions.question: The work done on an object by a force is defined as:
options: FΔx cos θ — force times displacement times the cosine of the angle between them
FΔt — force times the time it acts
The energy stored inside the force

questions.question: A force acting perpendicular to an object's displacement does:
options: Zero work, no matter how large the force is

questions.question: A crate is dragged 5 m by a 50 N horizontal force. The work done by the applied force is:
Friction of 20 N acts on that crate over the same 5 m. The work done by friction is:

subtopics.title: Net Work from the Free-Body Diagram

questions.question: Net work on an object can be found by:
options: Adding the magnitudes of all the forces
Adding the work done by each force with signs, or applying FnetΔx cos θ
Multiplying the largest force by the displacement
Ignoring forces that do negative work

questions.question: For the crate pulled with 50 N against 20 N of friction over 5 m, the net work is:
Negative net work on an object means the object:
options: Slows down — energy is being drained from its motion

questions.question: An object dragged at constant velocity has a net work of:
options: A positive value that grows with distance
A negative value set by friction
A value equal to the applied force
Zero — the positive and negative work balance

questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals:
options: The change in its kinetic energy

questions.question: A net work of 150 J is done on a 10 kg crate starting from rest. Its final speed is:
A 1 000 kg car at 20 m·s⁻¹ stops in 50 m. The average friction force, found via the theorem, is:
The work-energy theorem is usually the better tool than equations of motion when the question gives you:
options: A distance over which forces act
Only the object's colour and shape

questions.question: On an incline of angle θ, the component of the weight acting ALONG the slope is:
A 20 kg crate is pulled up a 30° incline at constant velocity against 30 N of friction. The applied force parallel to the slope is:
Over 4 m up the slope, the work done by gravity on that crate is:
Since the crate moves at constant velocity, the net work over the 4 m must be:
options: Zero, because the kinetic energy does not change
512 J, the work of the applied force

questions.question: Holding a 50 kg bag of cement perfectly still for ten minutes does:
options: A large amount of work, because it is exhausting
Zero work on the bag, because there is no displacement
Work equal to the bag's weight

questions.question: Carrying the bag horizontally at constant height does zero work on it because:
options: The upward force is perpendicular to the horizontal motion

questions.question: Lowering the bag gently to the ground, your hands do:
options: Negative work — the upward force opposes the downward motion

questions.question: In the bank account picture, the account balance stands for the object's:
Doubling a car's speed multiplies its kinetic energy by:
options: Four, because kinetic energy grows with the square of speed

questions.question: With the same braking force, a car at double the speed needs:
A question that gives you a stopping DISTANCE is inviting you to use:
Compared with lifting a fridge straight up, rolling it up a long gentle ramp to the same height requires:
options: Less force and less total work
The same force over a shorter distance
Less force but the same total work against gravity

questions.question: The work done against gravity in reaching a platform depends on:
options: The vertical height gained, not the length of the path

questions.question: A long gentle ramp can cost MORE total energy than a short steep one because friction:
options: Charges per metre of surface travelled

questions.question: Pushing the fridge up the ramp at constant speed means your work went into:
options: Nothing, since the speed never changed
Height gained and heat from friction, with no change in kinetic energy
